evidence: Abstract: evaluation on semi-structured Danish interview transcripts shows code-level coverage broadly comparable to human annotations, highly rated justifications, and a more compressed thematic structure
Section 5: final dataset of 99 transcripts (94 development / 5 test); analytical units defined as two consecutive question-answer pairs; segment-size trade-off 'was not systematically evaluated'
Section 6: Mistral 7B v0.3 Instruct used for interpretative tasks; inference configured deterministically; outputs constrained via Pydantic schemas implemented with Outlines (Section 6.1)

Section 7: analysis is 'exploratory and relies primarily on descriptive statistics rather than significance testing'; Section 7.2 uses two independent expert evaluators with randomized, blinded 5-point Likert ratings
Table 6 (Section 8.1): LLM produces 10 themes vs 19 for the human, mean 46.7 vs 20.79 codes per theme, largest theme 148 vs 54 (n=291 segments)
Section 8.2 / Figures 6-7: mean code coverage 3.40 (LLM) vs 3.13 (humans, n=33); justification quality 3.80 vs 2.73 (n=28), averaged over two evaluators on 5 segments

Section 9: limitations include limited evaluation sample, single small open-weight model, reliance on one human analysis for full workflow comparison, and theme quality not independently assessed; no code or artifact availability is claimed anywhere in the paper
llm_evaluation.rationale: In-scope LLM methodology paper: centrally about LLM-supported qualitative text analysis with prompting strategies, constrained/structured decoding (Outlines + Pydantic), and privacy-preserving local deployment of Mistral 7B, matching LLM, prompting, NLP, and structured-output/local-LLM preferences; not a pure domain application. Contribution is a coherent five-principle workflow design with a sensible interpretive/deterministic separation and a transferable evaluation framework, but novelty over prior LLM-TA work (De Paoli 2024; Montes et al. 2025) is incremental. Rigor and evidence are limited: only 5 test transcripts, a single human full-workflow reference, 2 expert evaluators, descriptive statistics only, unsystematic segmentation choice, and theme quality not independently assessed; the compressed-theme result (10 vs 19 themes) is a design artifact the authors themselves attribute to Phase 2 sequencing. Generalizability is claimed but shown on one Danish corpus and one small model; prompts are described but not fully specified and no code/data release is stated, hurting reproducibility.

primary_link.title: Designing an Auditable LLM-Supported Workflow for Qualitative Thematic Analysis

radar.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) offer new possibilities for scaling qualitative analysis, but existing applications often provide limited methodological transparency regarding how qualitative methods are translated into computational procedures. This paper presents an auditable and privacy-preserving computational operationalization of inductive and latent Thematic Analysis (TA). This paper first derives five design principles from the methodological requirements of TA and the conditions introduced
radar.summary_zh: 本研究針對大型語言模型(LLM)應用於質性研究時缺乏方法論透明度的問題,提出一套可稽核且保護隱私的主題分析(Thematic Analysis, TA)計算操作化流程。作者由 TA 方法論要求與 LLM 推論特性歸納出五項設計原則:保留詮釋脈絡、維持實證資料與分析產出間的可追溯關係、明確呈現分析建構與推理、將 LLM 推論限定於詮釋性任務,並支援本地部署以保護隱私。研究提出兩階段概念驗證工作流程:第一階段將訪談片段編碼並產生明確的分析理由,第二階段透過迭代式多對一映射將編碼聚合為主題,以確定性程式控制搭配受限的 LLM 推論,並以本地部署的 Mistral 7B v0.3 Instruct 執行。評估以丹麥半結構式訪談逐字稿進行,結合與人類分析的結構比較及獨立專家評分。結果顯示,工作流程的編碼覆蓋度與人類標註者相近(平均 3.40 對 3.13),分析理由品質更獲較高評分(3.80 對 2.73);但生成的主題結構較為壓縮,主題較少且範圍較廣(10 個對 19 個),反映第二階段循序設計促成早期主題聚合。研究限制包括評估樣本規模小、僅使用單一小型開放權重模型、完整比較僅依賴單一人類分析者,且主題品質未經獨立評估。此研究證明可稽核的 LLM 輔助質性分析確實可行,其模組化設計可擴展至更大型資料集並跨領域轉移,對兼顧效率與方法論嚴謹性的質性研究深具參考價值。

links.title: On the Design of Qwen3.8-Next Architecture: Evaluation, Efficiency, and Training Stability

evidence: Abstract: the model 'leads the 397B-A17B predecessor on eight' of fourteen pre-training benchmarks 'at 1/3 the activated parameters, 1/3 the training tokens, and roughly 1/9 the training FLOPs'.
§2.1.1 Table 1 (Architecture Ablation): GDN hybrid averages 53.81 across nine benchmarks vs 51.15 (SWA hybrid) and 49.87 (full attention) for matched 25B-A3B MoE checkpoints trained on 480B tokens.
§2.1.2 Table 3: with QSA, RULER beyond 512K improves 90.08→93.00 and 8-needle MRCR at 512K improves 30.66→40.53 vs the full-attention baseline.
§2.2 Table 5: GR reaches loss 1.590 and 54.66 average benchmark score vs pre-norm baseline 1.617/50.91 and mHC (dynamic) 1.594/54.47; loss-benchmark divergence explicitly discussed.

§3.3 Stress Test Results: at 4x optimal learning rate the AdamW baseline spikes 183 per 10k steps and crosses the clip threshold 213/19,932 steps, while both Muon runs never cross the threshold and Muon+GR records zero loss spikes.
§4 Table 11: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Base (125B total/6B active) outperforms Qwen3.7-Plus-Base (397B/17B) on 8 of 14 benchmarks (e.g., MMLU-Pro 73.23 vs 70.90, SWEBench-Pretrain 50.99 vs 49.24).

§2.1.1 Kernel Efficiency: 'The implementation and benchmarks are available at https://github.com/QwenLM/FlashQLA'; no comparable release of model weights, full training code, or data mixture is stated anywhere in the document.

§2.3.2 Table 9: n-gram vocabulary scaling lowers loss monotonically (1.585→1.526 from None to 200x) 'while downstream performance does not follow the same trend', an honestly reported negative result.
§3.2 Batch-Size Warmup: two ramp variants underperform the constant-batch baseline by 2.5e-4 and 3.5e-4 and 'requires 18.8% more optimizer steps'.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A core LLM architecture paper squarely within curatorial scope: sparse MoE design, hybrid linear/full attention (GDN), sparse attention (QSA), gated residuals, n-gram embeddings, Muon optimization, scaling laws, and stability — hitting multiple high-weight preferences (LLM 2.5, Transformer 1.2, Training/Optimization 1.5, Inference 1.5, Long Context 1.8). Novelty is moderate: each component refines known prior art (GDN from Qwen3-Next, DSA-style sparse attention, HC/mHC residual family, Gemma-3n-style n-gram memory, Muon), with the contributions being micro-block indexer compression, an elementwise-gated read, and a systematic three-axis (loss/benchmarks, cost, stability) evaluation methodology. Rigor is strong: matched-compute ablations at 25B-A3B scale (Table 1), verified scaling-law predictions at sensitive regimes (§3.2, Figs. 8-9), stress tests at 2x/4x LR (§3.3), exact branch decomposition (Fig. 7), and honestly reported negative results (n-gram vocab saturation in Table 9, sparse writes degrading post-training, warmup costing 18.8% more steps). Evidence is detailed and internally consistent but self-reported; several key results live only in figures. Reproducibility is limited: FlashQLA code is linked (§2.1.1) and much training detail is given, but no model weights, full training code, or data mixture release is stated.

On fourteen pre-training benchmarks the model leads the 397B-A17B predecessor on eight and trails it on the rest by at most 2.6 points, at 1/3 the activated parameters, 1/3 the training tokens, and roughly 1/9 the training FLOPs. Token mixing uses a layer-wise hybrid of
top5.summary_zh: 本文闡述 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 的架構設計與消融實驗。此模型為稀疏混合專家（MoE）架構，總參數 125B、每 token 僅啟用 6B，另以 51B 的 n-gram 嵌入表存放於主機記憶體，以近乎零額外運算擴充容量。作者主張損失、下游基準、效率與訓練穩定性應視為單一設計問題，逐項評估每個候選變更。Token 混合採 Gated DeltaNet（GDN）與全域注意力逐層混合，每四層僅一層全注意力；續訓階段以 Qwen Sparse Attention（QSA）取代，透過壓縮輕量索引器以 micro-block 粒度挑選上下文；殘差流拓寬為四分支並以逐元素閘門讀取，稱為 Gated Residual（GR）。搭配 Muon 最佳化器並重新擬合超參數縮放律，驗證更大的批次大小與學習率，且批次大小 warmup 已無必要。主要證據：十四項預訓練基準中八項領先 397B-A17B 前代，其餘落後至多 2.6 分，訓練 FLOPs 約為其 1/9；1M 上下文時 QSA 於 prefill 加速 7.6 倍、decode 加速 4.9 倍；壓力測試顯示新配方在四倍最佳學習率下仍穩定，全程無損失尖峰，亦無需 qk-clip 等顯式控制。論文亦指出損失與下游指標可能背離（如擴大 n-gram 詞彙只降損失、稀疏寫入在後訓練後劣化），並坦言評估吞吐量是未來最緊的瓶頸。此工作展示架構、效率與最佳化聯合求解的設計方法論。

links.title: When Errors Become Memories: Causal Pathway Tracing in Multi-Turn Memory-Augmented LLMs

evidence: Abstract: 'Question Repair reduces residual error by 27.5%, Memory Repair by 70.2%, and Joint Repair by 98.3%, nearly eliminating residual propagation.'
Section 3: first-order Markov assumption over rounds; two error entry pathways defined as memory-update A^{r-1}->M^r->A^r and question-feedback A^{r-1}->Q^r->A^r.
Section 5 Dataset Construction: '144 multi-turn interactions across six memory categories, with 24 instances each... one target error is injected at turn 3 and traced over the following 12 turns.'
Section 5 Valid Instances and Statistical Reporting: 125 valid instances for Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and 120 for OLMo3-7B-Instruct; 95% percentile bootstrap CIs from 5,000 resamples; 8 NVIDIA H200 GPUs.

Section 5.1 Evaluator robustness: Qwen-GLM full re-evaluation of 35,280 outcomes with 91.9% agreement and kappa 0.709; 're-judging preserves the direction of all 72 TPE estimates and yields temporal-curve correlations of r=.975-.996'.
Section 5.4: held-out instances show larger question-feedback pathway effects associate with greater Question Repair gains (rho=0.335, 95% CI [0.158,0.493]).

Section 5.3: MemoryBank-style consolidation vs episodic Top-3 retrieval comparison shows mechanism-dependent persistence ('episodic retrieval retains the erroneous entry... persistently high memory-state effects').
No code or dataset availability statement appears in the provided text (Sections 5-6); dataset details deferred to supplementary material not verifiable here.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Highly on-preference work: memory-augmented LLM agents, causal/interpretability-style pathway analysis, and reliability-adjacent safety concerns all match top-weighted topics. The contribution is a structural causal model decomposing cross-turn error propagation into memory-update, question-feedback, and interaction effects via a 2x2 counterfactual trajectory design (Section 4), which is a genuinely fresh angle beyond storage/retrieval-quality memory benchmarks, though adjacent to cited error-tracing work (MemTrace, memory-poisoning studies). Rigor is solid: formal estimands (TPE, PE_M, PE_Q, PIE), four outcome levels, two answer models, two memory mechanisms, six memory categories, filtered valid instances (125/120), bootstrap CIs, and a multi-judge robustness check (35,280 outcomes re-judged with GLM-5.2; 900 stratified with GPT-5.5; 91.9% agreement, kappa 0.709). Evidence quantitatively supports the headline claims (e.g., restoration reductions 27.5%/70.2%/98.3% in Table 2; held-out rho=0.335, CI [0.158,0.493]). Weaknesses cap the score: a small self-constructed dataset of 144 synthetic interactions with a simulated user (Qwen2.5-32B), only 7B-scale models, single error injection at turn 3, a first-order Markov simplification acknowledged in Section 3, reliance on LLM-as-judge proposition-level outcomes without human validation, no explicit limitations discussion, and no stated code or data release.

primary_link.title: When Errors Become Memories: Causal Pathway Tracing in Multi-Turn Memory-Augmented LLMs

top5.summary: Long-term memory enables large language models (LLMs) to preserve and reuse information across interactions, but it can also turn localized errors into persistent risks. Existing work mainly evaluates whether memory systems store and retrieve information correctly, leaving limited understanding of how errors propagate across responses, memory states, and future interactions. We propose a structural causal model (SCM)-based framework for cross-turn error propagation in memory-augmented LLMs. We m
top5.summary_zh: 長期記憶讓 LLM 能跨對話保留並重用資訊,但局部錯誤一旦被寫入記憶,便可能持續影響後續回應。本文提出以結構因果模型(SCM)為基礎的框架,分析記憶增強 LLM 的跨輪錯誤傳播:將使用者提問、模型回應與記憶狀態建模為動態因果過程,並識別兩條錯誤進入路徑——內部記憶更新與外部問題回饋。透過 2×2 反事實介入設計,作者定義總傳播效應、記憶更新路徑效應、問題回饋路徑效應與交互效應,並從記憶保留、自然回應、診斷探測與機率層級錯誤偏好四個層次衡量影響。實驗以 Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct 與 OLMo3-7B-Instruct 執行 144 段多輪對話、涵蓋六種記憶類別。結果顯示錯誤影響隨互動距離衰減,但記憶更新路徑比問題回饋更持久;錯誤即使從自然回應中消失,仍可能潛藏於記憶或生成偏好之中。不同記憶類別與機制(如 MemoryBank 與情節檢索)呈現相異的傳播模式。路徑引導修復實驗中,Question Repair 僅降低 27.5% 殘餘錯誤,Memory Repair 達 70.2%,Joint Repair 則達 98.3%,幾乎消除殘餘傳播。研究局限包括仰賴模擬提問與 LLM 命題級評估者、樣本規模有限,並採用一階馬可夫抽象。此框架為長期記憶系統的錯誤診斷與修復提供因果基礎,對部署可靠的長期對話代理極具價值。
top5.title: When Errors Become Memories: Causal Pathway Tracing in Multi-Turn Memory-Augmented LLMs
top5.title_zh: 當錯誤成為記憶:多輪記憶增強 LLM 的因果路徑追蹤

links.title: ECLIPSE: Self-Evolving Stealthy Prompt Injection Attack against Long-Horizon Agentic Systems

evidence: Abstract: claims up to 96.7% ASR without defense and 69.2% under a safety filter, exceeding the strongest baseline by 27.5% in the defended setting.
Section 6.2, Table 2: defended DeepSeek ASR 69.2% vs ObliInjection 41.7%; GPT-4o 62.5% vs ToolHijacker 59.2%; Claude 4.8 Opus 62.4% vs 0.8% for the best defended baseline.
Section 6.3, Tables 5 and Figures 4-5: prompt-only variant yields 19.2% ASR; SWE alone 66.7%; SWE+DTC 69.2%, isolating the tool-side steering contribution.
Section 4 and Appendix B: LASE-Bench has 120 tasks and 198 tools, 96.7% of tasks require at least five tool calls, constructed via benign synthesis plus 5-run stability filtering (>=4/5 passes kept).

Section 6.1 (Victim Agents/Implementation): results rely on unverifiable model names (GPT-5.6 Luna, Claude 4.8 Opus, Claude Sonnet 5, Kimi-k3-7b, QWEN-3.8-27b), single seed 100, temperature 0.0, N=120 per condition, no variance or significance reporting.

Section 6.4: case-study claims cite OpenClaw 387.4k stars / 2.18M weekly npm downloads and Hermes 235.9k stars / 5M Docker pulls with 2026 access dates; ECLIPSE achieves 61.7% (OpenClaw) and 55.8% (Hermes) defended ASR.

Section 7: defense analysis reports DataSentinel leaves 85.8% ASR, Tool-Guard 52.5%, AgentDoG 43.3%, SecAlign 0.8% ASR with 0.0% defense rate attributed to model-level refusal not counting as runtime interception.

Open Science section: commits to releasing code, LASE-Bench, tool pool, and plotting scripts; anonymized repository at anonymous.4open.science during review; injection prompts tuned for deployed agents deliberately withheld.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Squarely on-topic for the highest-weighted preferences (LLM agents, agent tool use/MCP, AI safety, red teaming/evaluation): it is an agentic prompt-injection attack and benchmark paper, not a domain application. Novelty is moderate-good: dual-channel (prompt+tool-description) injection with Static Workflow Encoding and Dynamic Trajectory Correction is a new combination over OPI/ToolHijacker/ObliInjection, and the long-horizon LASE-Bench (120 tasks, 198 tools, 96.7% tasks with >=5 calls, Section 4) fills a real gap, though components build on known primitives and 'self-evolving' is oversold iterative refinement. Rigor is solid in-document: formal verification conditions (Eqs. 7-10), five baselines under a unified harness, prompt- and tool-level ablations (Table 5: prompt-only 19.2% ASR vs SWE+DTC 69.2%), two case studies (OpenClaw, Hermes), and defense analysis (Section 7); deductions for single seed (100), no variance/significance reporting, and a single LLM-based filter for main defended results. Evidence strength is discounted because headline results depend on unverifiable/nonstandard victim models (GPT-5.6 Luna, Claude 4.8 Opus, Claude Sonnet 5, Kimi-k3-7b, QWEN-3.8-27b) and ecosystem statistics (OpenClaw 387.4k stars, Hermes 235.9k stars, Section 6.4) that cannot be externally checked, and 2026-dated citations. Generalizability is decent: 7 victims, 2 benchmarks, 2 native agent frameworks, 7000+ tool pool, though all within the authors' sandbox. Reproducibility claims are detailed (seed, temperature 0.0, implementation stack, anonymous repo, Open Science section) but rely on closed-source APIs and an unverifiable link, with tuned prompts deliberately withheld.

primary_link.title: ECLIPSE: Self-Evolving Stealthy Prompt Injection Attack against Long-Horizon Agentic Systems

top5.summary:
Recently, large language model (LLM) agents, such as Codex, Claude Code, and OpenClaw, have become capable of planning and executing long-horizon tasks through repeated tool calls. This capability also creates new opportunities for prompt injection. Existing attacks either place the malicious objective in one explicit instruction, making it easy to detect, or distribute the intent across multiple execution stages, making successful completion unreliable.
  In this work, we propose ECLIPSE, a sel
top5.summary_zh: 本文研究大型語言模型（LLM）代理在長時程任務中的提示注入安全議題。作者指出現有攻擊面臨兩難：將惡意目標集中於單一明確指令雖可控但易被偵測；將意圖分散於多個執行階段雖隱蔽但成功率不穩定。為此，論文提出ECLIPSE框架，在攻擊者可控制部分工具描述與提示的前提下，結合直接的使用者提示注入與間接的工具端注入。其包含兩大元件：隱蔽攻擊軌跡合成（SATS）於沙盒中產生並反覆驗證候選工具鏈，再將通過驗證的鏈渲染為自然的單次提示；工具鏈導引（TCS）則透過靜態工作流程編碼（SWE）在目標工具描述中嵌入狀態轉移線索，並以動態軌跡修正（DTC）在執行偏離計畫時提供修正訊號。為支持系統性評估，作者另建置LASE-Bench，含120個惡意任務與198個獨特工具，96.7%的任務至少需五次工具呼叫。實驗涵蓋七種代理與多款開源及閉源模型，顯示ECLIPSE在無防禦時攻擊成功率最高達96.7%，常見安全過濾器下為69.2%，於有防禦情境領先最強基準27.5個百分點；在OpenClaw與Hermes等真實代理系統的案例研究亦證實其可轉移性。侷限方面，軌跡監控類防禦（如AgentDoG）可將成功率降至43.3%，模型層級對齊（如SecAlign）更低至0.8%，且攻擊成效受各模型規劃與工具選擇行為影響，但整體而言現有防護皆無法可靠攔截。此研究凸顯須跨提示、工具描述與執行軌跡進行聯合推理的防禦需求，對代理安全深具警示意義。

top5.title_zh: ECLIPSE：針對長時程代理系統之自我演化隱蔽提示注入攻擊

links.title: Will the User Ever Know? Covert Indirect Prompt Injection on Tool-Using LLM Agents

evidence: Abstract & Section 5.2: ICoA achieves highest CSR on all four target models on AgentDojo with gains of 3.79–12.01 pp over 'Imp. message'; Table 1 confirms (e.g., LLaMA-3.3-70B CSR 23.81% vs 11.80%).
Section 3.2: transition-state analysis of n=2087 successful baseline traces shows overt successes mostly EXIT (70.92%) and covert successes mostly RETURN (67.70%), motivating the mechanism.
Section 5.4 / Table 2: appending the RETURN anchor to baselines raises CSR in every case, up to 23.71 pp (ChatInject on LLaMA-3.3-70B: 2.63%→26.34%).
Appendix C.1 / Table 4: leave-one-out ablation on LLaMA-3.3-70B — removing user framing drops ASR 32.46→21.92; removing RETURN anchor drops CSR 23.81→13.17, separating firing vs return roles.
Appendix F.2 / Table 7: judge validated on 500 stratified traces across GPT-4o, Claude Haiku 4.5, and human annotators; covert counts within ~1 and rank order preserved.
Appendix C.5 / Table 6: InjecAgent data-stealing suite (n=544) shows ASR/CSR rankings diverge (ChatInject CSR 0.00 at ASR 45.96%; ICoA CSR 29.60%), supporting cross-benchmark consistency.
Limitations: authors state LLM judge with incomplete human coverage across defense conditions, ReAct-only scope, and single-turn AgentDojo focus — bounding generalizability.

Appendices B.1, E, F.1, H: verbatim payload, judge prompt, defense formats, AgentDojo v0.1.34, temperature 0, and hardware/API cost details support reproducibility; no explicit code-release commitment.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM-agent security work: indirect prompt injection on tool-using agents, agent hijacking, prompt-injection defenses, and a new evaluation metric (CSR/OSR) — directly matching high-weight preferences (Agents & Tool Use, AI Safety, Red Teaming & Evaluation, LLMs). Novelty is genuine but bounded: the covert/overt decomposition of ASR and the ReAct RETURN/EXIT trajectory insight are new contributions, while the ICoA attack itself is a hand-crafted payload template with no learned or optimization component. Rigor is solid: 4 target models, 4 baseline attacks, 5 defenses, full AgentDojo (n=949) plus an InjecAgent generalization check, leave-one-out ablations, utility analysis, and judge validation against a second LLM and 500 human-labeled traces; however, no significance testing and the core disclosure flag rests on an LLM judge with incomplete per-condition human verification (Limitations). Evidence is internally consistent (e.g., claimed 3.79–12.01 pp CSR gains match Table 1 values exactly; ChatInject's high-ASR/low-CSR gap is corroborated on InjecAgent with CSR 0.00 at ASR 45.96%). Generalizability is limited by ReAct-only loops, single-turn interactions, and AgentDojo-centric evaluation — all acknowledged. Reproducibility is good (verbatim payload, judge prompt, defense formats, AgentDojo v0.1.34, temperature 0), though artifact release is only promised after provider notification and no code guarantee is given.

primary_link.title: Will the User Ever Know? Covert Indirect Prompt Injection on Tool-Using LLM Agents

top5.summary: As LLM agents take real-world actions through tools, indirect prompt injection (IPI) has emerged as a serious threat. The standard metric, Attack Success Rate (ASR), counts whether an injection succeeds but ignores what the user notices in the agent's final response. Looking at successful injection traces, we find two distinct outcomes: the agent executes the injection while returning an otherwise normal response, or reports the injected action in its final response, giving the user a chance to
top5.summary_zh: 本論文從使用者視角重新檢視工具使用型 LLM 代理的間接提示詞注入（Indirect Prompt Injection, IPI）風險。現行標準指標攻擊成功率（ASR）僅判斷注入任務是否被執行，卻忽略使用者能否從代理的最終回覆察覺攻擊。作者將 ASR 拆解為隱蔽成功率（CSR，攻擊成功且回覆不留痕跡）與公開成功率（OSR，使用者可察覺），並分析成功軌跡，發現關鍵差異源自 ReAct 迴圈的結構：注入後若代理返回使用者任務再結束，最終回覆便不會揭露攻擊；若軌跡停在注入動作上，攻擊就會被寫進回覆。據此，作者提出 ICoA 攻擊，在單一工具觀察結果中結合「使用者框架」與「RETURN 錨點」，先冒充使用者下達後續指令以促使注入執行，再誘導代理回到原任務，刻意製造隱蔽結果。在 AgentDojo 基準的四個目標模型（Qwen3-235B、LLaMA-3.3-70B、GPT-4o-mini、Gemini-2.5-Flash）上，ICoA 達到最高 CSR，較最強基準提升 3.79 至 12.01 個百分點；RETURN 錨點可直接附加於既有攻擊，最多提升 CSR 23.71 個百分點，且在偵測器、提示防禦與執行期任務對齊等五種防禦下仍保持領先。限制方面：隱蔽與否由 LLM 裁判判定（已與人工標註比對但未涵蓋所有防禦情境）、僅測試 ReAct 式迴圈、且限於 AgentDojo 的單輪互動。本研究的意義在於證明 ASR 不足以衡量代理安全，攻擊可被設計成隱形，防禦評估應將 CSR 納入考量。

links.title: The Safety Relay in Roleplay Jailbreaks: A Component-Resolved Causal Analysis of Harm Recognition and Refusal

evidence: Section 4.3 / Table 1: held-out assistant-start subtraction raises refusal from 0.6% to 78.6% (complete wrapper) and 44.1% to 81.2% (scenario), while equal-norm random directions change mean refusal by at most 1.2 points
Section 3.5 / Appendix G: reproducible development/evaluation split via SHA-256 hashing with seed 20250711; direction, block, and strength frozen before evaluation on held-out requests
Section 4.2: repair raises refusal to 100% and ablation suppresses up to 96.8% of refusals, localized to blocks 10-12 (Llama), 13-18 (Qwen), 17-28 (Gemma) (Appendix I)
Section 4.5: shared component carries 78.9% of squared norm; refusal-reference-parallel components produce gains of 38.3 and 25.3 points vs total edits of 42.5 and 27.7 (Appendices M-N)

Limitations: authors concede edits also increase benign refusal ('explanatory probes, not defenses'), later geometry reuses evaluation data without independent replication, and findings cover only two English benchmarks, three model families, four authored wrappers
Ethical Considerations: 'executable artifacts should be shared with appropriate access controls' — no confirmed public code or matched-prompt dataset release
llm_evaluation.rationale: Strongly in-scope LLM safety/interpretability paper: mechanistic analysis of roleplay jailbreaks on open-weight LLMs (Llama-3.1, Qwen2.5, Gemma-2), touching AI safety (2.0), red teaming/evaluation (1.8), interpretability (1.8), and LLMs (2.5); no Japanese-specific or out-of-scope domain content. Novelty is a genuine but incremental advance: component-resolved causal analysis of roleplay wrappers extends established refusal-direction (Arditi et al.) and activation-steering methodology to wrapper construction, with the 'safety-relay attenuation' framing as the main new concept. Rigor is high: matched harmful/benign pairs, four authored wrappers with labeled segments, reproducible SHA-256 dev/eval split frozen before evaluation (Section 3.5, Appendix G), sign/position/random-direction/transfer controls, and bootstrap intervals. Evidence is strong and consistent across 2 benchmarks x 3 models (Table 1: +78.0 refusal for complete-wrapper subtraction vs +1.2 random control), though GPT-5.1 judging with author-verification fallback is only partially validated and some cohorts are small (14-237 pairs). Generalizability is limited by English-only benchmarks, ~8B open models, and four authored wrappers, though transfer tests are positive. Reproducibility is good on protocol detail (seeds, strengths, blocks, wrapper templates in Appendix B) but no explicit code/artifact release; the ethics section only says artifacts 'should be shared with appropriate access controls'.

primary_link.title: The Safety Relay in Roleplay Jailbreaks: A Component-Resolved Causal Analysis of Harm Recognition and Refusal

top5.summary: Large language models are trained to follow instructions while refusing harmful requests. Jailbreaks exploit this balance to elicit content a model would ordinarily reject. Roleplay jailbreaks are especially concerning: the harmful request can remain visible inside a roleplay wrapper made of a persona, scenario, and task, yet the model may comply. We use mechanistic interpretability to determine how this context reverses refusal and which elements contribute to the reversal. Across two benchmark
top5.summary_zh: 本文研究角色扮演越獄如何逆轉大型語言模型的安全拒答:有害請求在由人設、情境與任務組成的包裝中仍然可見,模型卻可能配合回答。作者運用機制可解釋性,在 AdvBench 與 HarmBench 兩個基準、Llama-3.1、Qwen2.5 與 Gemma-2 三個模型家族及四個自撰包裝上,為每個有害請求人工配對良性對照,於請求與答案起始兩處量測殘差流的有害-良性方向,定義有害性保留(HR)與拒答傳遞(RT),以修復與消融介入定位因果區塊,並為完整包裝建構、情境框定及前綴×情境交互作用估計操作方向,在獨立保留的評估請求上進行減除測試。結果顯示:成功攻擊在請求層仍保有有害-良性區辨,但該訊號在答案起點明顯減弱,作者稱之為安全接力衰減,兩組 RT 差距為 0.149 至 0.209;減除完整包裝方向使拒答從 0.6% 升至 78.6%,減除情境框定方向從 44.1% 升至 81.2%,等範數隨機方向對照幾乎無效;效果具方向與位置特異性,並可跨包裝、跨基準遷移;兩個穩健方向平均 78.9% 的平方範數位於共享軸,且與無角色扮演時的一般拒答結構高度對齊。限制包括僅涵蓋英文基準、三個開源模型家族與四個包裝,部分失敗對照組過小,且編輯同時提高良性請求的拒答,故屬解釋性探針而非防禦。本研究指出:角色扮演未必抹除危害辨識,而是削弱辨識結果對答案的控制力,未來防護應維持從危害辨識到拒答的連結。
